documents.title: UMass Dartmouth Guidelines on the Use of Generative AI
documents.stance_why: The document sets a default of "students are prohibited from using GAI" absent "explicit permission or syllabus policy of an instructor", i.e. banned unless permitted, and only "encouraged" faculty to write syllabus statements; it offers no tiers, so restrict rather than delegates.
documents.summary: Faculty Senate guidelines that define generative AI, require students to disclose and attribute AI use, and bar presenting AI-generated work as one's own. Students may not use AI unless an instructor or syllabus permits it; faculty are encouraged to write syllabus statements.

units.why: The opening says the policy will "center the human" in education and research; a statement of purpose and principles for the whole document, so P56 (framework/preamble).
units.anchor: firmly center the human as both agent and object of university education

units.why: States the policy aims to "reaffirm existing university policies around academic integrity", so AI use falls under existing integrity rules; P77 (existing university policy) fits better than P45 because no collaborator analogy is drawn here.
units.anchor: reaffirm existing university policies around academic integrity

units.why: The aims list says the guidelines "Articulate fair-use and prohibitions on GAI use by students, faculty, and staff", stating the document scope and who it binds; P56 (scope and purpose).
units.anchor: Articulate fair-use and prohibitions on GAI use by students, faculty, and staff

units.why: Defines generative AI as "machine learning models that can generate text, images, code, and other content", fixing what the policy covers; P61.
units.anchor: machine learning models that can generate text, images, code, and other content

units.why: Says GAI refers to "all these tools and other generative computing not yet available", a scope clause extending the definition to future tools; P61.
units.anchor: all these tools and other generative computing not yet available
units.frag_start: The UMass Dartmouth Guidelines on the use of Generative AI uses

units.why: Claims the tools "mimic, rather than replace or even imitate" human work and "do not have analytical or critical capacities"; a rationale about what AI is, nearest P96 (AI is not a person or author) though it is not about authorship rules, hence fit_note.
units.anchor: they are not original or creative; they do not have analytical or critical capacities
units.frag_start: However, it is crucial to recognize
units.fit_note: Argues AI lacks creativity and critical capacity; it does not say AI cannot be an author or source.

units.why: States tools "often reinforce bias and spread inaccurate or incorrect information", naming bias and inaccuracy; P53 for bias, while P31 (verify output) is not chosen because no instruction to verify is given.
units.anchor: they often reinforce bias and spread inaccurate or incorrect information

units.why: Warns tools "can also provide a false sense of security or ease as users handover their own critical and creative faculties"; reliance on AI gives false confidence and cedes thinking, P43.
units.anchor: false sense of security or ease as users handover their own critical and creative faculties
units.fit_note: Concerns false security and surrendering critical faculties generally, not mastery exposed on exams.

units.why: "Faculty are encouraged to include a statement of their policy for AI use in their courses" recommends rather than requires a syllabus statement, so P09 with modality should.
units.anchor: Faculty are encouraged to include a statement of their policy for AI use

units.why: The aims list says the guidelines "Suggest ways faculty might clarify acceptable and prohibited AI use in syllabi and to their students", so they help instructors explain rules to students; P66 (explain rules to students), not P04 because no delegation sentence is stated here.
units.anchor: Suggest ways faculty might clarify acceptable and prohibited AI use in syllabi
units.fit_note: A stated aim of the guidelines to suggest wording ideas, not a rule on instructors.

units.why: "Some assignments might explicitly ask for the use of or engagement with GAI" says some assignments may call for AI use, P79; it states a possibility, so unit_stance permit.
units.anchor: Some assignments might explicitly ask for the use of or engagement with GAI

units.why: "students should follow the instructions of individual instructors and courses" makes the rule instructor- and course-specific, P04 rather than P78 because the emphasis is on instructors setting the rule.
units.anchor: students should follow the instructions of individual instructors and courses
units.frag_start: As with other assignments, students should
units.fit_note: Also tells students to follow each course instructions (P78).

units.why: "Absent explicit permission or syllabus policy of an instructor, students are prohibited from using GAI" states what applies when the syllabus is silent (P06); it also sets prohibition by default (P01) but P06 is more specific.
units.anchor: students are prohibited from using GAI
units.frag_start: Absent explicit permission or syllabus policy

units.why: "Students should always attribute and explain any usage" tells students to attribute and explain AI use, a disclosure duty, P24.
units.anchor: Students should always attribute and explain any usage

units.why: "Students must disclose the use of AI technologies in the creation of any coursework" is a mandatory disclosure with each submission, P24.
units.anchor: Students must disclose the use of AI technologies in the creation of any coursework
units.frag_start: Students must disclose the use of

units.why: "This disclosure should include a description of the GAI's role in the work" specifies what a disclosure contains; nearest P25 (tool, prompt, output) but it asks for the AI role, hence fit_note.
units.anchor: This disclosure should include a description of the GAI's role in the work
units.fit_note: Requires describing the AI role in the work, not the tool, prompt or output.

units.why: "Students must use GAI technologies responsibly and ethically, avoiding any form of misuse that could harm others or give an unfair advantage" is a broad conduct rule; P74 fits partly (harmful use), hence fit_note.
units.anchor: avoiding any form of misuse that could harm others or give an unfair advantage
units.frag_start: Students must use GAI technologies responsibly
units.fit_note: Broad duty to avoid harm or unfair advantage, not specifically deception or fabrication.

units.why: "This includes respecting copyright laws and the rights of others" ties AI use to copyright law, P52.
units.anchor: respecting copyright laws and the rights of others

units.why: "students cannot be required to provide their information or original work to third parties" protects student data when AI use is required; P50 (protect personal data).
units.anchor: students cannot be required to provide their information or original work to third parties

units.why: "faculty must take care, when requiring the use of GAI, to protect students' identities and original work" binds faculty who require AI; privacy of students, P50, not P79 because it conditions rather than allows requiring.
units.anchor: faculty must take care, when requiring the use of GAI, to protect students’ identities
units.frag_start: faculty must take care, when requiring

units.why: "students and faculty are required to attribute source material ... that has been generated by GAI" treats AI output as a source "As with any source (human, textual, creative, artificial)"; the operative rule is attribution, P24.
units.anchor: students and faculty are required to attribute source material, including text, image, code
units.fit_note: Also treats AI like any other source (P45) and binds faculty as well as students.

units.why: "Failure to do so is evidence of academic dishonesty" makes non-attribution itself evidence of dishonesty; P28 (nondisclosure is the violation) is closer than P36.
units.anchor: Failure to do so is evidence of academic dishonesty

units.why: "Students should always follow both the Student Handbook and the course syllabus in understanding how to attribute sources" sends students to the handbook and syllabus for attribution rules, P78.
units.anchor: follow both the Student Handbook and the course syllabus in understanding how to attribute sources

units.why: "The use of GAI technologies must not violate the principles of academic integrity" makes AI use subject to integrity rules, P36 (misconduct) since the focus is academic integrity.
units.anchor: The use of GAI technologies must not violate the principles of academic integrity
units.frag_start: The use of GAI technologies must
units.fit_note: States the standard but names no process or sanction.

units.why: "AI-generated content must be properly cited" is a citation duty, P24; the same sentence adds that AI use must not constitute plagiarism.
units.anchor: AI-generated content must be properly cited
units.frag_start: AI-generated content must be properly cited,
units.fit_note: Also says AI use must not constitute plagiarism or academic dishonesty (P36).

units.why: "students should never present work generated by GAI as their own original work" forbids submitting AI-generated work as one's own, P19.
units.anchor: students should never present work generated by GAI as their own original work
units.frag_start: Following an understanding of academic integrity,

units.why: "from low-stakes to high-stakes student work" extends the ban on presenting AI work as one's own to all levels; a scope clause of P19 kept separate, so fit_note.
units.anchor: from low-stakes to high-stakes student work
units.fit_note: Scope clause: covers low-stakes and high-stakes work and all intellectual, technical and creative processes.

units.why: "Use disciplinary or instructor guidelines for attribution" tells students to follow discipline or instructor attribution rules, P78.
units.anchor: Use disciplinary or instructor guidelines for attribution

notes: Copy hosted on newbedfordlight.org, not umassd.edu. The default-prohibition sentence appears in square brackets in the source, possibly an editorial insertion.
